conflicts.where: Part 2 prompt (a)/(c) vs Part 2 exemplar and Lesson 7 learned
conflicts.problem: Lesson 7 says 'reducing any one of these conditions slows or prevents spoilage', but the Part 2 exemplar says the samples cannot show which single condition mattered. The exemplar's claim is the sounder one. Lesson 7 also treats the six container conditions as if they separated the factors. The lessons do not teach this limitation, so the exemplar and rubric rely on a controlled-variable critique the lessons never taught.

The exemplar says drying omena and salting meat 'reduce the water available'. Lesson 7 claims these practices reduce 'water availability and temperature', and temperature is not reduced by drying or salting. Part 3 correctly states only water, but Lesson 7 is scientifically wrong.

Lesson 2 asserts that all the fuzzy patches are fungal mould, and Lesson 5 names Rhizopus, Penicillium and Aspergillus as the species. Lesson 5 claims species-level identification that the exemplar says was never done in class ('we did not identify them in class'). The lessons contradict each other on whether the species were identified.
